messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Text: Common side effects:
Common side effects of metformin hydrochloride tablets include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, wind (flatulence), indigestion, and headache.
These side effects occurred in 5% or more of patients.
The patients were in the US clinical trial.
The trial was for using metformin for type 2 diabetic patients.
In the same study, 6% of patients discontinued metformin due to diarrhea.
Less common side effects were abnormal stools, hypoglycemia, myalgia, lightheadedness, dyspnea, nail disorder, rash, increased sweating, taste disorder, chest discomfort, chills, flu syndrome, flushing, and palpitation.
These side effects occurred between 1% and less than 5% of patients.
Taking your medicine with meals can help reduce these side effects.
You may find the slow-release tablets reduce gastric side effects.
Tell your doctor if the side effects bother you a lot.
Tell your doctor if the side effects last for more than a few weeks.
Tell your doctor if the side effects come back after they've gone away.
Tell your doctor if the side effects start later in therapy.
Triplet: ["metformin hydrochloride tablets", "tested in", "US clinical trial"]

The relation 'tested in' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject drug was evaluated in the clinical trial specified by the object entity.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. B. 'has therapeutic index': The subject drug has a specific therapeutic index, which is a measure of its safety and efficacy, specified by the object entity.
C. 'used after': The subject drug is used following the treatment or condition specified by the object entity.
D. 'has clinical importance for': The subject drug has clinical significance or relevance to the medical situation or process specified by the object entity.
